Katalog Berita (Halaman 47/57)

#2145. Ancelotti e Raphinha espulsi in amichevole, Brasile ko con il Giappone: cos'è successo

Il Brasile ha vissuto delle montagne russe di emozioni, la doppietta di Vinicius Jr avrebbe sistemato le cose solo temporaneamente perché il Giappone alla fine ha prevalso allo scadere per 3-2 nel segno di Sakamoto. Era un'amichevole, in ordine allo Stadio Nazionale di Singapore, dopo un inizio piuttosto pigro della Seleção per 20 minuti e il 2-0 dei nipponici, con un Carlo Ancelotti parecchio irritato dalla situazione. Poi il risveglio al 33' con la stella del Real Madrid, un golazo sotto l'incrocio e un'altra splendida rete nel secondo tempo, ma non è bastato.

La remuntada del Brasile non è arrivata solo perché un bolide di Endrick ha scheggiato il palo del Giappone all'80', mentre Sakamoto ha anche infierito, approfittando di una deviazione in area per scavalcare il portiere verdeoro Pedro Morisco con un pallonetto e firmare il 3-2. Un'azione, tuttavia, che ha portato in escandescenza la panchina della Nazionale di Ancelotti.

Il Brasile chiedeva all'arbitro Jansen Foo di fischiare un fallo su Joao Gomes all'origine dell'azione. A causa delle forti proteste, il direttore di gara ha espulso Carlo Ancelotti e anche Raphinha (Barcellona). Il VAR ha poi rivisto l'azione, concordando con la decisione del fischietto in campo. In questo modo, la terza rete giapponese è stata convalidata subito dopo e la Seleçao è caduta. Adesso i verdeoro torneranno in campo martedì prossimo per l'ultimo test amichevole contro Singapore.

#2144. Birmingham City have a number nine problem to solve when August Priske returns from injury: Opinion

Birmingham City have plenty of reasons to be optimistic about their Championship promotion push, but Jay Stansfield’s recent performances could prove particularly significant. The 23-year-old scored twice against Swansea City, including an 87th-minute winner, to send BCFC top of the table.

He also passed 50 goals for the club before his 24th birthday, underlining his importance since arriving as their record signing. However, it is not just his finishing that makes Stansfield so valuable.

His recent return to the central striker position suggests Chris Davies may have found the best way to get the most out of his €18m-rated forward. However, it may cause an issue with top-scorer August Priske returning from injury.

Across 15 starts and 1,275 Championship minutes this season, Stansfield has registered four goals and one assist, averaging a 7.26 FotMob rating. His 42 shots, 20 efforts on target and 4.88 expected goals demonstrate a consistent appetite for getting into dangerous positions.

Stansfield has frequently operated in attacking midfield during his Birmingham career, but his historical numbers make a compelling argument for keeping him further forward. In 71 appearances as a striker, he has scored 29 goals. By comparison, 46 outings as an attacking midfielder have produced just 12 goals.

That difference is particularly relevant with Priske recently absent. Stansfield has stepped into the central role and responded with three goals across the Millwall and Swansea fixtures, despite accumulating just 1.09 xG in those matches. Against Swansea alone, he registered seven shots and earned a 9.1 FotMob rating.

Crucially, playing centrally does not mean sacrificing his work rate. Stansfield has recorded 39 defensive contributions, including 22 tackles, eight interceptions and 65 recoveries this season.

He is not a conventional target man, winning just 28.6% of his aerial duels, but his mobility, pressing and ability to link play make him a different kind of centre-forward. FotMob’s positional data also highlights why moving him deeper is not necessarily beneficial.

His shot volume and defensive contributions are strengths, whereas his relatively low touches suggest he is not someone who needs to dominate possession to influence matches.

Birmingham invested heavily in Stansfield because of his goalscoring ability, and his record already justifies that faith. With a contract until 2031, there is little reason to reinvent his role.

Priske’s eventual return could give Davies another attacking option, but Stansfield should remain the first-choice striker. The recent evidence suggests Birmingham have a better chance of maximising their record signing when he is leading the line rather than supporting someone else.

#2143. Cardinale: "Non venderò mai il Milan. Voglio vincere e non posso tollerare che..."

Cardinale: "Non venderò mai il Milan. Voglio vincere e non posso tollerare che..."

Installa la nostra App gratuita e accedi più velocemente alle notizie

Mentre navighi nell'app, scorri il dito da sinistra a destra dello schermo per tornare alle pagine precedenti

Di certo l'ambizione a Gerry Cardinale non manca. Quanto consapevole sia, eventualmente lo si scoprirà nel tempo. Perché almeno a parole il proprietario del Milan non sembra avere intenzione di mollare. Lo racconta alla Gazzetta dello Sport, spiegando cosa lo ha portato a lanciare una nuova holding a Milano:

�La forza trainante dietro a operazioni come questa è fornire al Milan la potenza finanziaria necessaria per competere sul mercato dei trasferimenti per assicurarsi i migliori giocatori al mondo. Trasformerò il profilo finanziario del club con le risorse che arriveranno dallo stadio, dall’arena a San Donato e dalle altre attività alle quali stiamo lavorando come Nba Europa. Sto facendo tutto il possibile per assicurarmi che, quando vogliamo un calciatore, nessuno possa dirmi: “Non puoi prenderlo perché non potete permettervelo”. Adesso solo le società della Premier League sono in grado di investire certe somme e di assicurarsi i top player. Se voglio riportare il Milan ai vertici nelle coppe europee, non soltanto in Italia, dobbiamo capire come poter competere con i club più importanti al mondo».

Questo progetto conferma che il suo impegno sul Milan è a lungo termine. «Sì. Non venderò mai il Milan. Mai. E questo è un progetto per farlo tornare a vincere. Non sono disposto a tollerare che per riuscirci ci voglia molto tempo. Voglio farlo il prima possibile. Vedremo quanto velocemente... Il mio obiettivo è conquistare scudetti con continuità e naturalmente tornare in Champions. Milan Sports & Entertainment rappresenta le fondamenta per rendere possibile tutto questo».

Un discorso a parte lo merita il legame con Milano: RedBird e la città ora sono ancora più legati. «Questa è l’eredità che lasceremo a Milano. Lo stadio, ovviamente, rappresenta un’eredità enorme che trasformerà il nostro profilo finanziario, ma poi ci sono anche il progetto dell’area a San Donato e il resto. Se vogliamo che il Milan torni grande bisogna colmare il gap di ricavi con le società della Premier. Quando ho comprato il club, quattro anni fa, ho usato l’espressione “Berlusconi 2.0” e nessuno ha capito quello che volevo dire. Adesso forse si inizia a vedere».

Si spieghi meglio. «Tutti pensavano che stessi facendo un paragone arrogante, egocentrico, tra me e Berlusconi, ma era quello il mio obiettivo. Quello che cercavo di spiegare era che, come Berlusconi aveva trasformato il Milan e insieme la Serie A, noi vogliamo essere, attraverso la nostra proprietà, capaci di portare la società nella nuova era in cui stiamo vivendo. E bisogna fare nello stesso modo in cui lo fece Berlusconi ovvero in un modo nuovo. Io sono abituato a lavorare in un certo modo perché agisco così, ai massimi livelli mondiali e in America».

La sua “ricetta” potrebbe essere valida anche per la Serie A? «Certo, anche per la Serie A. Secondo me non sarebbe stato un buon affare vendere il 30% dei propri diritti commerciali internazionali quando è arrivata l’offerta di JP Morgan. Non è così che la Serie A può tornare al vertice in Europa. Bisogna farlo attraverso la pianificazione aziendale e creando tutte le opportunità per creare nuovi ricavi. Come faremo noi con Milan Sports & Entertainment. Saremo i primi a realizzare (assieme all’Inter, ndr) uno stadio dal 2011 e questo è un risultato enorme. Ho cominciato a lavorarci da quando ho comprato il Milan e finalmente è arrivato... il momento giusto».

#2141. Italia ad Appiano: Doumbia al posto di Frattesi ma ci possono essere sorprese. Tutte le ultime

Ultime sull'Italia direttamente da Appiano, che ospita l'allenamento della Nazionale azzurra alla vigilia della sfida di Nations League contro il Belgio (in programma domani a Bruxelles). Con Frattesi che ieri ha lasciato il ritiro (nulla di grave per il centrocampista della Lazio), il ct Mancini ha fatto diverse prove di formazione mescolando le carte.

Doumbia, conferma Sky Sport, potrebbe essere il sostituto dello stesso Frattesi, con la conferma di Barella mezzala e Tonali centrale. Attenzione a centrocampo però anche all'alternativa Fagioli, che nel caso andrebbe a sostituire Barella.

In mattinata - riporta invece la Federcalcio - lo staff medico azzurro ha valutato le condizioni di Nicolò Cambiaghi: l’attaccante del Bologna non ha recuperato dal trauma alla caviglia riportato giovedì in occasione della partita con la Francia e lascerà quindi il ritiro. In difesa, Mancini ha provato Palestra come terzino destro, e può dunque essere un nome da spendere al posto di Kayode. Infine, per quanto riguarda l'attacco, con Cambiaghi out, a sinistra ci può essere l'opzione Dimarco avanzato. Con Vergara a destra che andrebbe dunque a giocare al posto di Sebastiano Esposito (ma non è da scartare nemmeno l'ipotesi Liberali).

Nel pomeriggio è prevista la partenza degli Azzurri per Bruxelles, dove domani - ricordiamo - affronterà il Belgio nell'ultima partita del girone di Nations League. In serata è prevista la conferenza di Mancini alle 19, seguita dalla visita di una delegazione alla targa commemorativa delle vittime della strage dell'Heysel.

#2140. Sebastiano Esposito, l’agente: “Ora non pensa al mercato, ma potrebbe giocare benissimo in un tridente con Hojlund e Vergara”

A Radio Napoli Centrale, nel corso di Un Calcio alla Radio, è intervenuto l’agente Mario Giuffredi: “Io vivo le partite dei miei assistiti con grande passione e coinvolgimento. Come se fossi con loro in campo. Durante la partita non riesco a essere distaccato, sono molto acceso. Dopo la partita, ritorna l’equilibrio. E riesco anche a essere più equilibrato delle critiche degli stessi calciatori. Come ho vissuto i due rigori degli Esposito? Non ho visto nessuno dei due rigori di Pio e Sebastiano. Ero anche a cena con Salvatore Esposito. Capivamo in base alle reazioni degli altri che erano con noi a tavola. Pio sentiva la responsabilità della partita. Aver segnato quel rigore contro la Francia toglieva il pensiero del rigore della Bosnia. Pio ha una lunga carriera, può migliorare statistiche con Nazionale e club. Io non guardo le pagelle, so come ragionano i giornalisti, che non si limitano a guardare la prestazione, ma anche episodi, dettagli. La prestazione di Sebastiano è stata saggia a livello tattico. Ha giocato in posizioni di campo non suoi. Mi dispiace che i giornalisti non si limitano a questo, ma si limitano a guardare il rigore sbagliato. Per sbagliare quel rigore, devi avere il coraggio di batterlo. Sull’1-1, contro quel portiere (Maignan ndr) e contro quella Nazionale, devi avere coraggio. Io mi ero arrabbiato con Sebastiano se non avesse avuto il coraggio di andare dal disco. Sebastiano Esposito e Vergara insieme con Hojlund? Si incastrerebbero benissimo, perché Sebastiano è un toro a livello fisico. Vergara ha grande forza nelle gambe. Hanno anche colpi tecnici, sono imprevedibili. Non sarebbe maschio. Però non facciamo i direttori del Napoli né gli allenatori del Napoli. Aiutare il Napoli portando Sebastiano Esposito? Io non mi sono mai sottratto ad aiutare il Napoli e mai lo farò. Al tempo stesso non sono io che vado a insistere per far prendere quel tipo di giocatore. Sono orgoglioso di quello che sono. Il fatto di essere arrivato dalla galetta mi rende orgoglioso. Negli ultimi due anni ho avuto la media di quattro giocatori convocati in Nazionale. Vedo che nel primo e nel secondo tempo ho due giocatori su tre in campo. Ieri sera dopo la partita, presa coscienza, ho preso l’auto e sono andato nei luoghi dove tutto è iniziato. Per un napoletano è tutto più difficile, ci sono tantissimi ostacoli messi davanti da invidiosi. Hai sentito Pio Esposito dopo la partita contro la Francia? Il futuro di Pio è all’Inter, senza dubbio. Sta benissimo. Il club ha mostrato sempre attacco e riconoscenza. Sebastiano si trova benissimo al Sassuolo, in questo momento non pensare neanche al mercato. Quello che succederà si vedrà. Entrambi stanno bene dove stanno. Pio sicuramente rimarrà all’Inter per tanti anni, è la sua seconda pelle; mentre Sebastiano magari si vedrà strada facendo se sia meritevole di alzare ancora di più il livello, ma è prematuro parlare di mercato.Il paragone di Pio Esposito con Meazza? Noi vediamo tutto con serenità ed equilibrio. Io vivo con questa concezione: ci addormentiamo la sera con la consapevolezza che il mattino possa finire tutto. Questo ci permette di non cullarci su certe cose. Il calcio è lo sport più bello e più crudo del mondo. Uno dei più grandi giocatori per me è stato Roberto Baggio. Lui a tratti viene dimenticato, nessuno gli ha dato un posto di un certo livello. Il calcio ha bisogno di gente come Roberto Baggio. Questo mi fa pensare che un giocatore verrà dimenticato in un secondo. Perciò bisogna vivere tutto con equilibrio. Qual è il prossimo che la mia scuderia ha in rampa di lancio? Te ne dico due. Quando dico le cose ci metto la faccia e vado anche controcorrente. Dico Favasuli e Marianucci. Per me Marianucci può arrivare in Nazionale, è un difensore di grandissimo livello. Ha qualcosa in più rispetto a tanti altri. Se migliora nell’attenzione, diventa di grande livello. Favasuli lo diamo per scontato, perché è partito bene”.

#2137. Wrexham should revisit Pavel Sulc situation after latest Lyon revelation: Opinion

Wrexham have had a very poor start to the season considering their finish to last year. However, they are a couple of strong January additions away from pushing themselves up towards the Championship play-off picture. One target could be a returning bid for Lyon’s Pavel Sulc.

Phil Parkinson’s side reportedly made the highest offer for the Lyon attacker in the summer of 2026, with their bid understood to be worth approximately £35m. However, Sulc rejected the opportunity, admitting he was not attracted by the prospect of playing in the Championship or moving to a small town in Wales.

That rejection appeared to end Wrexham’s hopes, but Lyon’s financial difficulties have created a potential second opportunity. The French club must sell players during the January window to satisfy financial commitments, and Sulc has emerged as one of their leading candidates for departure.

The 25-year-old has established himself as an exciting attacking talent since joining Lyon from Viktoria Plzen for an initial €7.5m in August 2025. Under contract until June 2029, he can operate as an attacking midfielder, striker or left winger, offering considerable versatility.

His underlying numbers also demonstrate why Wrexham were prepared to spend so heavily. He has 11 goals and three assists in 27 Ligue 1 appearances during his first season at Lyon.

He has also made an encouraging start to 2026/27, registering one goal and three assists in five league appearances, alongside another goal in the Europa League.

His creativity is particularly appealing. Sulc recorded eight chances created in just 417 Ligue 1 minutes this season, while his ability to contribute goals from several attacking positions would address one of Wrexham’s biggest weaknesses.

Parkinson’s side have struggled for attacking consistency, with injuries to Sam Smith, Josh Windass, Nathan Broadhead and Callum O’Hare leaving them short of creativity and firepower. Sitting around 15th in the Championship, they need reinforcements if their promotion ambitions are to remain realistic.

There are, however, two significant complications. Sulc underwent surgery on a meniscus injury in October, with his return potentially falling anywhere between January and March. Lyon’s reduced negotiating position could also make a deal more affordable, although his injury represents a genuine availability risk.

His previous comments about the Championship and Wrexham’s location cannot be ignored either. Nevertheless, the club’s continued investment and ambitions could offer a different proposition several months later.

Wrexham should not assume Sulc has changed his mind, but the sporting circumstances and Lyon’s financial position have shifted. Given their need for attacking quality, reopening the conversation would certainly be worthwhile.

#2135. Avellino, il sindaco Pizza a D’Agostino: “Non accettiamo ricatti, non subiamo pressioni”

Botta e risposta a distanza sul futuro dello stadio dell’Avellino. Il sindaco Nello Pizza ha risposto con toni duri alla conferenza stampa in cui il presidente biancoverde Angelo D’Agostino ha presentato il progetto del nuovo Partenio-Lombardi, un impianto UEFA 4 da 21mila posti. Il primo cittadino ha respinto le accuse e ha annunciato che il Comune illustrerà alla città la propria posizione definitiva entro due settimane.

Pizza chiarisce di non aver partecipato alla presentazione “per ragioni di doverosa imparzialità istituzionale”: “Parliamo di un bene pubblico - si legge su TuttoAvellino -, di soldi pubblici e la mia partecipazione ad una iniziativa volta alla presentazione del progetto di una delle parti interessate sarebbe stata sbagliata ed irrispettosa”. Poi la risposta ai toni usati dal presidente del club: il sindaco parla di “le minacce e i ricatti che non c’intimidiscono” e ribadisce: “Noi non accettiamo ricatti, non subiamo pressioni, non ci pieghiamo a diktat”. Il sindaco rivendica la correttezza dell’amministrazione e rimanda al mittente l’accusa di strumentalizzazione: “sono ormai otto anni che si fa campagna elettorale sullo stadio senza che si sia arrivato a un risultato concreto”. Per Pizza, inoltre, “non esiste e non è mai esistita alcuna contrapposizione tra il Comune e l’U.S. Avellino”.

Sul merito dell’opera il sindaco frena: “La realizzazione di uno stadio è un’operazione finanziaria rilevante e complessa”. L’avvio di una conferenza di servizi, aggiunge, “non garantisce la copertura finanziaria dell’opera e non ne determina automaticamente la realizzazione”. E ancora: “I tempi li detta il pubblico, li detta la legge, li dettano le procedure”. Pizza spiega che sono in corso “approfondimenti giuridici, tecnici, amministrativi ed economico-finanziari” e che nella prossima settimana, “tutt’al più in quella successiva”, il Comune sarà pronto a illustrare “le risultanze del lavoro svolto e la posizione definitiva del Comune”.

Il sindaco ricorda che “il Comune non dispone di risorse proprie per un investimento di tale portata” e per questo definisce il confronto con la Regione Campania “fondamentale, anzi indispensabile”. Pizza cita le recenti parole del “Presidente Fico”, che “ha confermato la volontà di finanziare il nuovo Stadio Partenio Lombardi sulla scorta del Documento di Indirizzo alla progettazione approvato dal Consiglio comunale”. Il traguardo comune, conclude, è “dotare Avellino di uno stadio moderno, funzionale e all’altezza delle aspettative della città, della provincia e dei suoi tifosi”.

Colonna Inter, invisibile per la Germania: Bisseck vuole tutto. Yann vuole far ricredere Klopp

Praticamente inamovibile nell'Inter, ma quasi invisibile per Klopp e la Germania. La strana storia in questa stagione di Yann Bisseck. Due strade fin qui parallele, che non hanno intaccato il rendimento in nerazzurro, una situazione che il difensore vive così, secondo il Corriere dello Sport:

"Attore protagonista nell’Inter, ma ancora alla ricerca di una propria dimensione nella Germania. Yann Bisseck è rimasto alla Pinetina dopo aver sperato di poter rientrare nelle convocazioni di Klopp. Il gigante nerazzurro era stato chiamato a settembre, quando il maxi gruppo dei convocati era stato suddiviso tra le quattro partite previste, ma stavolta ci è rimasto male e Klopp non è ancora pienamente convinto, preferendogli per il pacchetto arretrato l’ex Milan Thiaw. Per Bisseck si tratta di uno stimolo in più per alzare ulteriormente il livello delle prestazioni, dopo che in questa prima parte di stagione è riuscito a imporsi con continuità con la maglia interista, strappando un ruolo da protagonista nel reparto arretrato".

"Di recente in zona gol ha sbloccato anche la sfida di Champions contro il Feyenoord e Chivu si fida ciecamente di lui, tanto da lanciarlo titolare per 8 gare su 11 in Serie A e 3 su 4 in campionato. Dopodiché a marzo l’ex Aarhus spera di rientrare nel giro della nazionale, in modo da entrare nel vivo di Euro 2028 con le relative qualificazioni al torneo. L’estate scorsa Bisseck ha rinnovato fino al 2031 ed è con la maglia dell’Inter che vuole diventare un difensore di spessore internazionale, dopo essere cresciuto nell’ultimo anno nelle vesti di braccetto destro e con la possibilità ulteriore di poter agire anche da difensore centrale. A 25 anni il tedesco sta entrando nel pieno della propria carriera ed è per questo che nei prossimi mesi punta a far ricredere anche Klopp, con l’obiettivo di diventare una presenza costante nella propria nazionale rispetto alle due sole partite maturate fin qui".

#2133. Napoli, occhi sempre su Zirkzee: duello con la Juve per Varela. Il punto di Mediaset

Negli ultimi giorni sono molti i nomi che sono finiti sul taccuino del ds Giovanni Manna. L’ultimo, quello di Joshua Zirkzee. Il Napoli continua a lavorare sul mercato alla ricerca di un rinforzo offensivo da affiancare a Hojlund. Il più seguito è Varela, ma arrivare al centravanti del Monza già a gennaio non sarà semplice. Le sue nove reti, che ne fanno il capocannoniere della Serie A, saranno fondamentali nella corsa salvezza della squadra di Juric. Privarsi del proprio attaccante più prolifico a metà stagione rappresenterebbe un sacrificio importante per il club brianzolo. Una difficoltà che spinge Manna a guardarsi intorno e a valutare anche soluzioni alternative.

Su Varela, intanto, si registra anche l’interesse della Juventus, dando vita a un possibile derby di mercato tra bianconeri e azzurri. Il Napoli segue e apprezza il 21enne portoghese: nelle scorse ore il club ha raccolto informazioni attraverso il suo entourage, approfondendo anche gli aspetti economici dell’operazione. La concorrenza e soprattutto il peso del giocatore negli equilibri del Monza rendono però la trattativa particolarmente complicata.

Ecco perché Manna sta battendo anche altre piste, con uno sguardo rivolto soprattutto alla Premier League, dove non mancano occasioni da cogliere. Una porta a Joshua Zirkzee, 25 anni, attualmente al Manchester United. L’olandese conosce bene la Serie A, dove si era messo in mostra nella stagione 2023/24 con la maglia del Bologna. Sotto la guida di Thiago Motta aveva realizzato 11 gol e 5 assist, contribuendo alla storica qualificazione dei rossoblù in Champions League. Numeri e prestazioni che avevano convinto lo United a investire 42,5 milioni di euro per portarlo a Old Trafford.

A Manchester, però, il percorso dell’attaccante ha subito una battuta d’arresto. In questa stagione ha trovato poco spazio, collezionando appena 186 minuti e due reti in dieci partite. Una situazione che potrebbe favorire un’eventuale partenza e trasformare l’olandese in un’opportunità nel mercato di gennaio. Il Napoli osserva e vuole provarci: l’olandese potrebbe rappresentare una soluzione per completare il reparto e offrire a Hojlund un compagno e ad Allegri un’alternativa con caratteristiche diverse rispetto all’attaccante danese.

Per arrivare a Zirkzee, però, il Napoli dovrà prima fare i conti anche con il mercato in uscita. Le posizioni di Lang e Lucca sono quelle da monitorare con maggiore attenzione: entrambi potrebbero lasciare spazio a nuovi innesti e diventare le prime pedine sacrificabili per fare cassa. Eventuali cessioni permetterebbero a Manna di recuperare risorse da reinvestire sul mercato e provare a dare concretezza all’ipotesi che porta all’attaccante dello United. La strada per Zirkzee passa dunque anche dalle uscite: il Napoli valuta le occasioni in entrata, ma prima dovrà trovare le condizioni economiche per affondare il colpo.

#2132. Lazio, Brentford su Isaksen: Lotito valuta il rinnovo fino al 2030

Il club inglese potrebbe presentare un'offerta a gennaio; per il danese si ipotizza uno stipendio da 2,5 milioni.

Il Brentford segue Gustav Isaksen e potrebbe presentare un’offerta alla Lazio nella prossima sessione invernale. Claudio Lotito non intende privarsi facilmente dell’esterno danese: la società valuta invece un rinnovo per trattenerlo.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

La Premier League guarda di nuovo alla Lazio. Secondo Tuttomercatoweb, il Brentford ha inserito Isaksen tra i propri obiettivi e sta valutando un tentativo per portarlo in Inghilterra. Si tratta, per ora, di un possibile assalto di mercato, non di una proposta già presentata.

Il club londinese è ottavo in campionato con 14 punti e considera il danese un profilo interessante per rinforzare l’attacco. Dopo un inizio di stagione difficile, il classe 2001 ha migliorato il proprio rendimento ed è diventato uno degli elementi più importanti della squadra biancoceleste.

In Serie A Isaksen ha raccolto 11 presenze, 4 gol e 1 assist. La sua crescita ha attirato attenzione anche fuori dall’Italia, ma per il Brentford arrivare a un accordo con la Lazio non sarebbe semplice.

Il club considera Isaksen importante sia per il presente sia per il futuro. Una partenza a gennaio indebolirebbe il progetto tecnico: per questo una proposta ordinaria non basterebbe a convincere Lotito a prendere in esame la cessione.

Soltanto un’offerta straordinaria potrebbe modificare la posizione del presidente. La Lazio punta a un piazzamento in zona Champions League e ritiene fondamentale il contributo dell’esterno danese per raggiungere quell’obiettivo.

#2131. Sheffield Wednesday injury update on Louie Barry pre-Plymouth Argyle clash

Sheffield Wednesday have been without the winger since early September due to an ankle injury. SWFC are back in League One action this weekend with a home clash against Plymouth Argyle at Hillsborough.

Barry, 23, was snapped up by the Owls over the summer on a permanent basis from Aston Villa and he penned a four-year deal with the South Yorkshire outfit until June 2030, with the option of a further 12 months on top of that. He has since made six appearances in all competitions this season and has chipped in with three goals and one assist.

In this latest update regarding his condition, his head coach Challinor has said, as per the official club website: “We hope to see him back certainly within the coming weeks. Maybe Saturday; we’ll see what the next few days look like.”

Sheffield Wednesday are positioned in 9th place in the table after their first 13 fixtures and they are two points off the play-offs behind Reading in 6th. They have drawn their last two league outings on the spin against Cambridge United and Blackpool.

Sheffield Wednesday will be looking forward to having Barry back. SWFC’s form hasn’t been great over recent times.

The Owls have won only one of their last eight matches in all competitions. Challinor knows Barry well from their time at Stockport County together and has managed to get the best out of him in the past.

Barry was signed by his current club in the last transfer window to bolster their attacking department. When fit, he will give them more competition and depth to pick from at the top end of the pitch.

The ex-England youth international was on the books of Aston Villa from 2020 to 2026. He played once for their first-team and was loaned out to Ipswich Town, Swindon Town, MK Dons, Salford City, Hull City and Sheffield United, as well as Stockport County, to get some experience under his belt and to boost his development.

Barry is a proven performer at third tier level and will inject some serious quality into Sheffield Wednesday’s starting XI. SWFC fans will be excited to see him back in action for them.

Challinor will be eager to get a win over Plymouth Argyle on Saturday afternoon. He has lost his first two outings against Oldham Athletic and Accrington Stanley in the FA Cup and EFL Trophy respectively.

The new Owls’ manager will get the chance to put his own stamp on his newly inherited squad with some signings in January. He will also have the opportunity to offload some players if needed.

#2130. Come svolta il calcio italiano? Falsini: "Un progetto tecnico rigorosamente individuale per tutti"

Gianluca Falsini, allenatore del Como, a TUTTOmercatoWEB.com parla così della crisi del calcio italiano e i come, a suo parere, si potrebbe aiutare i giovani ad imporsi anche in Serie A dopo la Primavera: "Bisogna avere un progetto tecnico rigorosamente individuale per ogni ragazzo. Lontani, Palma e Liberali sono delle eccezioni, non la regola. Faccio un esempio con due nostri ragazzi: Liberali e Papaccioli. Dopo il gol in Champions League, a Papaccioli fecero l'intervista e poco dopo anche a Liberali, e lui rispose da adulto: "Sono contento per lui, era la prima volta che giocava, gli ho fatto l'assist...". Eppure Liberali ha un anno in più rispetto a Papaccioli... ma un percorso completamente diverso: ha fatto la Serie C col Milan, poi sei mesi da titolare in Serie B a Catanzaro e poi è andato al Como, perché è un talento purissimo. Ogni giovane ha i suoi tempi e le sue tappe. I 2007 che giocano oggi in Primavera, se hanno avuto un anno di stop per infortunio come è capitato ad altri, fanno bene a restare sei mesi, ma già a gennaio dovrebbero andare a misurarsi con i grandi, magari in Serie C o in Serie D. Le seconde squadre sono fondamentali, ma serve anche un progetto, un programma su misura: l'intensità delle partite che vedo in Youth League è molto vicina al calcio dei grandi. Tenere un ragazzo in Primavera solo per vincere lo scudetto giovanile significa bruciargli un anno di maturazione calcistica".

L'importanza della Youth League: "La Youth League è un'esperienza incredibilmente formativa. Giochi contro formazioni e atleti individualmente superiori alla media del campionato Primavera 1, che è già un ottimo torneo. Si confronta con una qualità vicinissima a quella della prima squadra. Senza contare la grande fortuna che abbiamo avuto quest'anno, grazie alla lungimiranza di Cesc Fabregas, che ha dato fiducia in Champions League a un nostro ragazzo come Papaccioli, che è andato pure a segnare. Quando affronti club come Lipsia, Lens, Manchester United o Feyenoord, ti rendi conto che il livello è completamente diverso rispetto alla Primavera 1. È un acceleratore di miglioramento straordinario".

#2129. Gattuso: “Sogno lo stadio pieno. Sugli infortunati…”

Ai microfoni di Lazio Style Channel, mister Gennaro Gattuso ha commentato la vittoria in amichevole contro il Mgarr United

Ai microfoni di Lazio Style Channel, mister Gennaro Gattuso ha commentato la vittoria in amichevole contro il Mgarr United.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Cosa mi porto dietro dall'amichevole di oggi? Che non si è fatto male nessuno (ride, ndr). Scherzi a parte, siamo molto soddisfatti. I moduli contano poco, è la mentalità e la voglia di far fatica in campo. Rovella e Cataldi avevano bisogno, anche Doekhi e Gudmundsson.

Secondo me si può fare, Nicolò è dinamico, ha bisogno di condizione e mettere minutaggio. Si è allenato bene, si è dato da fare.

Lunedì faranno le risonanze Nuno, Zac e Frattesi, bisogna aspettare per vedere l'entità dei danni. Per questo stiamo temporeggiando, Zac sta già facendo qualcosa sul campo. Per Sutalo e Marusic aspettimo ancora un po' di giorni e usciremo con un comunicato quando saremo sicuri delle diagnosi.

I principi non cambiano, anche se ogni giocatore ha le sue caratteristiche. Servono intensità e voglia, così come oggi anche se era un'amichevole. Anche gli altri hanno infortunati, non dobbiamo piangerci addosso.

Deve fare uno switch, ci ho parlato ieri, ha età e potenziale. Deve migliorare sotto porta, stiamo lavorando, può fare molto di più.

Parlo e mi scontro molto con lui, può diventare uno dei migliori invasori del mondo. Io ogni volta che rubavo palla li contavo e per me erano tutti gol, sapevo che intorno avevo giocatori che con la palla erano più bravi di me. Lui è fondamentale, ma la differenza la stiamo facendo sull'attacco alla linea, ma non lo sta facendo solo lui. Arriva a fari spenti, non è un caso che sta facendo tutti questi gol. Ci scanniamo, ma ci vogliamo bene.

Il calcio è cambiato, le dinamiche che ho vissuto io da calciatore oggi non vanno più bene e devi sempre trovare la chiave giusta per entrare nella testa dei calciatori. Io non riesco a recitare, ho capito fin dal primo giorno dove venivo, sapevo che ci mettevo poco ad affezionarmi alle persone che sono qui, ai tifosi, al club. La storia della Lazio è incredibile, la gente è malata per la Lazio e poi ci rimani, il mio sogno è vedere la mia squadra con uno stadio pieno, festeggiare sotto la curva. Il calcio senza tifosi non è calcio, è qualcosa di diverso, i nostri tifosi sono coerenti e difficilmente torneranno, ma noi dobbiamo onorare la maglia. La speranza è l'ultima a morire. Gudmundsson? Non è brillantissimo, ma ha grandi giocate, ringraziamo che non ha avuto ricadute.

Neymar torna a far parlare. #2127. ‘Encouraging’: Scotland media rave about Stoke City player after North Macedonia win

The Scots won 2-1 at Hampden Park in their latest National League outing and have risen up to 3rd in the Group E table. Aston Villa midfielder John McGinn scored twice for Sebastien Pocognoli’s side as they secured an important three points.

Graham, 22, was handed his first start for his country and his second cap and he caught the eye. He was snapped up by Stoke City in the summer on a four-year contract from Dundee running until June 2030 and he has since adapted well to life in the Championship.

Journalist Anderson was impressed by the centre-back’s display against North Macedonia and delivered his verdict, as per a report by the Edinburgh Evening News: “Making his first start, he looked composed in the heart of defence. Scotland are back in action on Monday evening as Graham eyes his third appearance. They face a tricky away trip to Switzerland as they target another positive result.

Stoke City landed Graham in the last transfer window to bolster their defensive department. He has since become a key player for SCFC.

At the age of 22, he has potential to grow and develop further down the line. He battles it out with the likes of Ben Wilmot, Bosun Lawal and Maksym Talovierov for game time with the Potters.

Graham has made 15 appearances for Mark Robins’ side in all competitions in this campaign, 13 of which have come in the league, and he has chipped in with one goal. He made his debut for Scotland off the bench against North Macedonia in early October.

The ex-St Johnstone academy man rose into Dundee’s first-team in 2024 after loan spells away from Dens Park at Lochee United, Albion Rovers and Montrose as a youngster to get some experience and to boost his development. He went on to make 46 outings for his previous team and found the net on three occasions before heading down the border to England when Stoke City came calling.

Stoke City’s swoop for Graham earlier this year has worked out well for all parties involved. SCFC’s summer recruit is now gaining international recognition with Scotland.

The Potters are joint-top of the table along with Birmingham City and Middlesbrough. They won 2-1 away at Portsmouth last time out.

Robins’ men are unbeaten in their last five games. They are back in action next weekend with a home match against Birmingham City.

#2126. Data estimates how much Huddersfield Town loan star Cameron Humphreys is worth ahead of potential permanent swoop

Huddersfield Town are the team to watch in League One this season. HTAFC sit 1st in the table and, despite a first-round exit of the FA Cup, will be hopeful of a return to the Championship.

The Terries have seen several outstanding performers with the likes of Derensili Sanches Fernandes and Joe Taylor. However, it’s Cameron Humphreys who has come to life in the 2026/27 campaign under Martin Drury.

Huddersfield Town signed the 23-year-old on loan for the second consecutive term in the summer, and he has established himself already with five assists in 13 games. If he continues at the same level, the Terriers may have to consider turning his spell into a permanent deal.

Humphreys is under contract at Ipswich Town until 2028, so if they cash in on the midfielder, they could demand a relatively substantial fee. However, given the fact he rose through the academy at Portman Road and would generate absolute profit, he could go for a cheaper fee.

That is what the data suggests, and Huddersfield Town would certainly entertain a move for the midfielder if his value is accurate. FootballTransfers value the youngster at €700,000, which is just under £600,000.

Given his displays in League One this season and the current market rate for most 23-year-olds in the ranks of a Premier League side, it wouldn’t be a surprise to see ITFC actually demand a seven-figure sum to acquire Humphreys.

The midfielder has won 57% of his duels this season and has won 32 fouls for HTAFC. With eight big chances created and 18 successful crosses, Ipswich Town will undoubtedly view his price tag as a lot higher should bids come in for him in 2027.

Huddersfield Town’s main chance of signing Humphreys comes down to whether or not Ipswich Town remain in the Premier League by the end of the campaign. The 23-year-old is excelling in League One this season, and if they were in the Championship again, the Tractor Boys would likely include him in their plans.

That being said, HTAFC currently sit top of the third tier, and promotion to the second tier would give them a great pull to sign the midfielder permanently. Drury has the Terriers playing a good brand of football, and if Humphreys were a part of his plans, there’s no reason why he wouldn’t want to join.

The 23-year-old has made just 44 appearances for Ipswich Town since his debut in 2021. However, since the 2023/24 campaign, he has appeared only 14 times for the Tractor Boys and his patience could be running out for a future at Portman Road.

#2125. To infinity and beyond! Another stunning Diego Gomez strike has Brighton up to SECOND and daring to dream... as Brentford's Igor Thiago is goaded into a red card

Published: 11:08 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 12:40 EST, 8 November 2026

Onwards and upwards go Brighton. Another victory to send them soaring into second place with only Arsenal above them.

It is a lofty perch for the Seagulls and one more admirable when considering the depths from which they have risen.

Homeless and penniless, on the brink of extinction at the end of the last century they are now daring to dream about the Champions League.

To infinity and beyond. Why not? Fabian Hurzeler’s team have already beaten Arsenal and Manchester City without conceding this season.

The only goals scored against them in the last six Premier League games came at Liverpool, where they lost 2-0 but were not outplayed.

City’s season is mired in uncertainty, awaiting sentence for financial breaches and the other half of the traditional Big Six are so erratic there will likely be scope for interlopers when the prized European tickets are handed out in May.

It is six months away but at this moment in time there are not four teams better than Fabian Hurzeler’s.

Brighton appear fully formed. Delightfully fluent in attack. Creative with zip and imagination and different ways to score goals.

There is a defined style of play. Solid at the back with enough sporting maturity to survive a test of needle, which this became against Brentford after the red card for Igor Thiago’s red card.

Diego Gomez celebrated another memorable strike at the Amex Stadium after his halfway-line stunner in the 5-0 win over Crystal Palace

The Bees already trailed to a screamer from the left boot of Diego Gomez and went further behind before half time when Pascal Gross converted a penalty awarded for a shirt pull by Keane Lewis-Potter on Luka Vuskovic.

Brighton (4-2-3-1): Verbruggen 6; Costinha 6, Dunk 6, Vuskovic 6, Boscagli 7; Gross 8, Andres 6 (Wieffer 46, ); Gomez 7 (Yalcoue 90+3), Ayari 7 (Hinshelwood 78), De Cuyper 7 (Minteh 82); Kostoulas 6 (Rutter 82)

Subs not used: Steele, Hadjam, Kadioglu, Svoboda

Bookings: Andres, Boscagli, Wieffer, Dunk

Brentford (4-3-3): Kelleher 6; Kayode 5, Ajer 6, Van den Berg 6 (Wilson 70), Lewis-Potter 5 (Diouf 59); Sangare 5 (Jensen 59), Janelt 5, Hickey 5 (Collins 46); Ouattara 4 (Yarmoliuk 46), Thiago 3, Schade 4

Subs not used: Valdimarsson, Anthony, Damsgaard, Schuster

Gross, the 35-year-old midfielder schemer who walloped his penalty into the top corner in emphatic fashion, embodies the confidence pulsing through this team and his goal closed the contest.

The Bees assembled in the deep looking to minimise damage with an eye on a counterattack or a set piece and maybe hoping the officials would see fit to even it up at 10 against 10.

It didn’t happen. Instead, Brighton controlled the ball. They have had more than 75 per cent of possession across 90 minutes and spent the second half probing around the fringes of the Brentford penalty area.

They registered 20 shots in all but there would be no third goal. And nobody minded. They celebrated the victory and a return to the Amex Stadium after five away games in a row and more than 5,000 miles on the road.

Every substitution made by Hurzeler came as a reminder of their strength and quality.

Kaoru Mitoma, yet to feature this season, is expected back from injury soon after the international break.

The Conference League is not proving a distraction to a squad of such depth and Hurzeler gave fans his permission to dream.

'They should be always excited,' said the Brighton boss. 'That’s our job. They can dream. They can have high expectations, but these are things we can’t control. We played good game but always things we can do better.'

This was Brentford’s second defeat in this Premier League season and they had players sent off in both.

'In both scenarios the opposition player has been the one to provoke the situation, antagonise our player and react towards our player in an aggressive way,' fumed boss Keith Andrews, referring to Yehor Yarmoliuk’s red card against Liverpool, when the Bees finished the game with nine men.

'We should do better, but the game is in a state now and a place I don’t particularly like. And we’ll have to have a look at that because it’s costing us.'

Chema Andres fouled Thiago, fell to the ground and sprang up to confront the Brazilian, who tried to push him away but caught him with a forearm under the jaw.

Igor Thiago's yellow card was upgraded to red after a VAR intervention

Andres collapsed for a second time. When Michael Oliver gave them a yellow card each it seemed fair, but VAR Stuart Attwell sent the referee to the pitch-side screens for a review.

Oliver studied the slow-motion replays and upgraded it to a red card. Off went Thiago, smiling wryly and shaking his head, dismissed for standing his ground and being goaded into a reaction.

He will miss games against Everton, Manchester United and Arsenal.

Opinions of Oliver in the away end did not improve when he gave a penalty for a shirt pull by 5ft 7in Keane Lewis-Potter which somehow sent 6ft 4in Luka Vuskovic somersaulting to the turf.

Vuskovic is already a favourite at the Amex Stadium and it is easy to forget he is only 19. He dominates in the air and reads the game like a seasoned central defender.

And after ten games he is ten points better off than those he left behind at Tottenham.

The Croatia international cannot be looking forward to yet another encounter with England. The two nations meet at Wembley on Thursday. England have put 11 past them in two games this year.

#2124. Femi Azeez signs: What West Brom’s perfect January transfer window looks like

When the January transfer window opens up, West Brom will be hoping they are still in the promotion mix to attract some desired targets.

The Baggies have been excellent under James Morrison so far this season, going into the latest international break unbeaten in their last six league games and securing four victories in that time.

Their latest 3-0 romping of Millwall last weekend leaves Albion fifth in the second-tier standings, sitting just one point off the summit in such a compact top eight.

It’s been a remarkable turnaround under Morrison, particularly when you factor in that the Black Country outfit underwent somewhat of a revamp this summer, recruiting 10 new players, many of whom had never played a minute in the Championship before their moves to The Hawthorns.

And with the Baggies setting their sights on ending a six-year exodus from the Premier League, showing ambition in the January window could be what gets them over the line in that quest.

All connected with Albion will be hoping it’s a statement window for bolstering key areas of the squad, with the attacking departments in particular still needing to be strengthened.

So, with this in mind, FLW has detailed three players West Brom should sign to make it a perfect January transfer window.

During the January transfer window, a department West Brom must address is on the flanks.

Starting off on the right-hand side, Femi Azeez could be a signing of intent given his previous Championship exploits with Millwall.

His heroics at the Den last season earned him a move to Premier League outfit Brighton, signing on the dotted line for a reported fee of £12.5m.

However, a hamstring injury means he is yet to feature for Fabian Hurzeler’s side, although Azeez is believed to be closing in on a return to full fitness.

However, with Brighton flying high in the Premier League, it’s hard to see where Azeez will fit in once he comes back, with Hurzeler not wanting to disrupt a team that is in full flow and playing so well.

Meanwhile, Yankuba Minteh is now back involved after his own injury issues, and, given his quality, he will presumably stay ahead of Azeez in the pecking order. Not to mention Kaoru Mitoma is scheduled to return this month as well, so it’s difficult to see the 25-year-old getting much, if any game time.

Baggies fans, would you welcome a loan move for Femi Azeez in January despite his fitness concerns? Comment below!

Therefore, a loan move may well be on the cards in January, and a return to the Championship could be exactly what Azeez needs to get back playing regularly and rediscover his old form.

After scoring 11 goals and registering eight assists from 35 Championship games last season, Azeez has proven to be such a livewire in the second tier.

And with the Baggies needing players to hit the ground running, Azeez is more than capable of doing that given his previous pedigree.

Azeez is a player who could add an extra gear to Albion’s attacking line, while the Black Country are in need of reinforcements there given Kareem Tunde is the only recognised right-winger on the books at this moment in time.

Over on the opposite wing, George Hemmings could be an ideal player to come in and share minutes with Mikey Johnston.

The Republic of Ireland international is yet to play a minute in the Championship so far after suffering a reoccurrence of his ankle problem that ruled him out of the majority of Morrison’s caretaker reign towards the end of last season.

He’s expected to return to the squad imminently but during the Christmas period and certainly over the new year, Albion are going to have to be careful with his minutes as they build up his fitness.

And a younger understudy could be the perfect arrival to come and take the burden off Johnston, with West Brom credited with interest in Hemmings by the Express & Star back in July.

The Villains ultimately didn’t sanction any exit due to Hemmings’ regular role in the first team at the beginning of the campaign, but further summer signings at Villa Park have since settled in and pushed him down the pecking order.

Hemmings came off the bench for 19 minutes of Villa's dramatic 4-4 draw with Manchester United last weekend, but hadn’t featured for the team in their previous four league matches, so the 19-year-old has a chance of heading for the exit door on loan in 2027.

While the Baggies haven’t had the most prosperous partnership with Aston Villa when it comes to loaning in their players, Hemmings has the potential to be a star in the Championship, with Unai Emery’s trust to throw him in for their UEFA Super Cup clash with Paris Saint-Germain and the beginning of their Premier League campaign speaking volumes about the talent he possesses.

Such a sharp and technically gifted player, Hemmings is another wideman who could have a massive impact on the potency of Albion’s forward line, and given their previous interest in securing his services, it’s a loan deal that could well progress when the January window opens.

As well as bolstering out wide, the arrival of another striker is what West Brom didn’t manage to do in the summer and something they must rectify in January.

The Baggies were busy during the summer window revamping some of the forward line, replacing the outgoings of Josh Maja and Daryl Dike with Barney Stewart and Jimmy-Jay Morgan.

Morgan in particular has been a roaring success so far, grabbing eight goal contributions in his opening 15 league matches for the club, but is not a conventional centre-forward, drifting over to the left-hand side while a proper number nine stays central.

Pundit Tom Garratt has urged the Baggies to do all they can to sign Andri Gudjohnsen in January.

In contrast, the more traditional centre-forwards, like Stewart, have found opportunities hard to come by, netting just once for his new club so far, while Aune Heggebo in his second season at the club has also found himself in and out of the side, with most of his success coming after being introduced from the bench.

Thankfully, much of Albion’s early success has been down to players in other positions chipping in with goals, but over time, that’s at risk of drying up, so Albion must do all they can at the turn of the new year to bring in a forward who has an eye for goal and can make a real difference when leading the line.

And a name that could well be on West Brom’s shortlist is Ellis Simms, who himself has struggled to gain regular minutes for Coventry City in the Premier League.

It won’t be a name that generates a lot of excitement among the Albion faithful, but after scoring 13 times in the second-tier last season, Simms has shown he’s a player who contributes goals in the Championship at a steady rate and could keep the Albion team ticking over with enough strikes to keep them in the promotion conversation.

At the same time, it’s a realistic deal for the Baggies to achieve, with the club likely to be eyeing up a loan deal for any striker in January after much of their budget went towards some of their summer rebuild.

Simms has only featured four times in the top-flight for the Sky Blues so far this term, and with a move to The Hawthorns not far away from his current employers, it would be a surprise to not see the former Everton frontman linked with a move to B71.

Proven at Championship level and physically suited to the division, Simms is a player Albion could depend on for the second half of the season, with the team needing that extra bit more at the top end of the pitch to keep up their high-flying start.

#2123. ‘Embarrassing themselves!’ Jamie Carragher hits back at Rio Ferdinand over Cristiano Ronaldo defence

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Jamie Carragher has taken aim at Rio Ferdinand for defending Cristiano Ronaldo following the Portuguese forward’s latest controversy with his national team.

Ronaldo has found himself at the centre of a growing dispute after abruptly leaving Portugal’s national team camp following a reported disagreement with head coach Jorge Jesus. The incident has prompted strong reactions from former teammates and pundits, with Ferdinand firmly siding with the Al-Nassr star.

Jamie Carragher, however, believes Ronaldo’s reputation should not shield him from criticism when his behaviour becomes difficult to defend.

Rio Ferdinand, who played alongside Cristiano Ronaldo at Manchester United between 2003 and 2009, criticised Jorge Jesus for the way he handled the situation.

Speaking on his Rio Presents podcast, the former United captain criticised Jesus for not showing respect to Cristiano Ronaldo.

“Cristiano Ronaldo was put in a very bad situation and was treated in an inappropriate way. He has an enormous history in football. Jorge Jesus did not deal with Ronaldo well and chose to treat him in that way, but I cannot find any explanation for it,” Ferdinand said.

Despite Jesus being Portugal’s manager, Ferdinand questioned his standing, comparing him with the likes of Sir Alex Ferguson and Pep Guardiola. To say the least, Ferdinand only embarrassed himself doing that.

Jamie Carragher saw the argument very differently and rightfully so.

Speaking on The Overlap Daily, the former Liverpool defender suggested that Ferdinand’s friendship with Ronaldo was influencing his reaction to the incident.

“People think it’s good to be close to people in the game, but this is where it becomes a problem,” Carragher explained.

He then called out both Ferdinand and broadcaster Piers Morgan, who has also been vocal in his support of Ronaldo.

“People like Piers Morgan and Rio Ferdinand, who are big people in the media whether you like them or not, are embarrassing themselves with the nonsense that they’re coming out with because they know Ronaldo. You can know someone and try to look after them, but you cannot defend the indefensible.”

Carragher believes Ronaldo’s achievements should not put the forward beyond criticism, particularly when his actions involve his national team and its management.

Gary Neville, who also played with Cristiano Ronaldo, has questioned Ronaldo’s handling of the situation, despite his longstanding affection for his former Manchester United teammate.

Neville argued that Ronaldo’s public response had made matters worse and the forward needed to accept criticism rather than expect others to defend him.

“With Cristiano, it’s difficult because I love him, but I can’t watch what happened at United in his second period and then see him make a statement like that without saying something. He has to be pulled up on that and told that it isn’t acceptable,” Neville said.

He also suggested Ronaldo’s extraordinary success, wealth and influence could have contributed to a sense that he was beyond challenge.

“When you have a billion pounds in the bank, the achievements he has had and the power he has, you feel you’re unbreakable, you feel you’re unstoppable,” Neville added.

Despite his criticism, Neville does not believe the episode will define Ronaldo’s legacy permanently. He expects the attention to fade once the forward retires, allowing his achievements on the pitch to take centre stage again.

#2122. 'He's got raw talent' - Notts County urged to plot shock QPR transfer raid ahead of January

Notts County have been steady so far in their first League One campaign since 2014/15, sitting 17th with 14 points in 12 games.

Given how difficult a start they've had on paper, it's been incredibly impressive to see how solid Martin Paterson's side has been defensively, despite being a newly promoted side. Only Huddersfield Town and Bradford City have a better xGA, while they've allowed the fourth-fewest shots and shots on target, too.

It's not all been perfect, though. While Notts have been brilliant at stopping shots, they haven't been excellent going the other way. They've scored just 13 times this season, with five of those coming in their last three.

Perhaps that could be an indication that things are starting to click up front, especially with Charlton Athletic loanee Daniel Kanu netting his first two goals for the club in that three-game stretch, but attacking firepower is, at the moment, top of the January wishlist when the winter window opens.

FLW's Notts County fan pundit, Gareth Parr, is still of the opinion that a striker is needed at Meadow Lane in January. Kanu has been sharing striker duties with six-foot-four frontman Luka Smyth, who also has a couple of goals, both against Burton Albion back in August.

Martin Paterson has started to get some joy playing them both alongside each other in this three-game unbeaten run, but if anything, that increases the demand for competition in those places.

Parr wouldn't mind Notts taking a look at QPR frontman Rayan Kolli, who has just recently returned to the Hoops fold after being unfavoured by Julien Stephan due to a perceived lack of effort.

Pick any two players. Send the code, and your mate enters it here to play the same pair.

"Notts desperately need a striker," he said. "And with that, you look one of two ways. Either older, proven and capable of scoring 15-20 goals, or a younger, developing one.

"I guess in terms of young and developing, Rayan Kolli at QPR is a promising youth prospect. Notts have dipped into the loan market regularly, and Kolli has been struggling to get into the QPR side, especially behind [Richard] Kone and [Rumarn] Burrell when they're fit.

"He's got raw talent, needs guidance, but could provide some interesting competition for Kanu and Smyth, who both seem to be struggling to find the net."

Kolli has been on the cusp of becoming a regular starter at QPR for a couple of years now. He netted four times in 819 minutes in the 2024/25 Championship campaign, and last season, scored five times in just over 1,000 minutes.

With the Hoops a much better chance-creating side this year in Julien Stephan's second campaign in charge at Loftus Road, it seemed almost inevitable that he could make that step-up.

For one reason or another, though, he hasn't been able to. Even now, with him back in the fold, he's yet to score, and after starting the first three games after the three-week international break, Kolli has failed to start any of the last four, and has been unused from the bench in two of them.

FLW gets AI to rank the friendliest clubs in the second tier this season

As Parr mentioned, the 21-year-old has Kone and Burrell ahead of him, but the latter is currently out injured, and yet he's still struggling to start regularly. Either Paul Smyth has been given the nod, or Stephan has gone with just the Ivorian as a lone striker.

Kolli needs a fresh start somewhere, even if it's just a change of scenery for a few months, which a loan spell in January would provide. Perhaps Notts County would be the perfect place for him to rediscover some form and get him back on track at Loftus Road.

Unfortunately for Notts, or any other League One side who may want to loan Kolli this upcoming January, QPR have a real history of injuries at the top end of the pitch, and that could make the Hoops lean towards keeping him just in case.

As mentioned, Burrell is currently out and has played just 14 league games in 2026 so far, following a lengthy lay-off in the second half of last season. Justin Obikwu is nowhere to be seen due to injury, and Alfie Lloyd has been in and out of the squad due to fitness, too.

If all of them are fit, alongside Kone and Smyth, Kolli may be seen as expendable. However, the likelihood of that happening seems slim, and even if it did come to fruition for a short time, you can't bank on the whole frontline options being available at the same time at Loftus Road.

Do you think QPR could be open to letting Rayan Kolli leave on loan this January? Let us know in the comments.

With Kolli being a strong depth option, QPR may be hesitant to let go of him at all in January, which could prove frustrating to Notts County if they decide to try and bring him to Meadow Lane.

#2121. Is Mainoo-Tielemans the right midfield option for Man Utd?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United drew 1-1 at home to Tottenham despite having an extra man advantage. The Reds saw Mbeumo put them in front, but Solanke scored a late leveller in injury time after Bentancur was shown a red card for headbutting Luke Shaw.

Manchester United’s worrisome season continues after accumulating just six points off the first six games, their first start in 40 years. But more than the results, what worries Manchester United is their midfield pairing.

United spent massively on their midfield rebuild and somehow can’t find the best combination in the midfield. Michael Carrick has gone with the Mainoo-Tielemans partnership, but they have failed to control the midfield. Individually, they both come with decent numbers, but collectively they fall short.

Mainoo and Tielemans struggled against Tottenham while closing the midfield and at times showed a lack of energy. On the day when nothing clicked for United, the Mainoo-Tielemans partnership particularly raised eyebrows.

Gary Neville has also raised serious concerns about Manchester United’s Mainoo-Tielemans partnership.

Neville was particularly unimpressed by the midfield balance, arguing that the problems went beyond one disappointing performance.

The former United captain stopped short of ruling out the combination altogether, but he suggested he has serious doubts about its suitability.

“Tielemans and Mainoo, I’m not calling time on it, that’s probably too drastic, but I’ve seen enough of it to think that’s not a midfield that’s dynamic enough to play at this football club in the Premier League.”

Former Spurs midfielder Redknapp felt United struggled to connect their midfield with the rest of the team during the opening stages.

He added: “I didn’t see enough connections in that midfield in the first hour. Baleba came on and did OK and showed a bit more.

“They look devoid of any confidence, any idea, any patterns of play, playing out from the back. Tottenham were much better than them in every single department.”

While Carlos Baleba was a particular highlight on the day, he showed great potential when brought on. He brought a new sense of energy in the midfield and sent a few balls over the top for a couple of quick counterattacks as well.

Redknapp also pointed to the physical demands of modern Premier League football, arguing that United cannot afford to be outworked by their opponents.

Tottenham ran a staggering 5 km more than Manchester United, something Redknapp felt was a pattern.

"Spurs ran 5km more than Man United… it's like that EVERY GAME!"Jamie Redknapp is less than impressed with the lack of ground covered this season by Manchester United 😬 pic.twitter.com/BxWkFuyGJ1

“There is a pattern that I don’t really like when I watch teams, and that’s when every time the stats don’t lie and the other team runs more than you.

“I feel in Premier League football right now there are a couple of non-negotiables, and one is you have to run more than the other team if you want to win or at least get close enough. Tonight Spurs ran 5km more than Manchester United.”

He believes Tottenham’s pressing exposed the lack of pace in United’s midfield, making it difficult for the hosts to move the ball safely through the centre.

“In terms of how they played today, I think they have an issue with Tielemans and Mainoo in midfield. I don’t see enough energy in there. Baleba will add a lot and will give them a tremendous amount of energy but right now, when things aren’t going well… and Tottenham knew it!

“Every time United played the ball out from the back they pounced. They pressed them because they knew United don’t have the pace and speed in midfield to get away.”

“In isolation, one of them is absolutely fine, the two of them together doesn’t work for me. They haven’t got the pace or the energy to get around the pitch for 90 minutes.”

#2120. One lesson Senne Lammens learned after Tottenham’s late equaliser

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Senne Lammens believes Manchester United must learn to finish games off after their late collapse against Tottenham Hotspur.

The result left the goalkeeper frustrated at Old Trafford despite leading the game and with a player more on the field.

Manchester United looked set for three points after Bryan Mbeumo put them ahead in the second half, but Dominic Solanke’s stoppage-time equaliser denied Michael Carrick’s side a much-needed victory.

Speaking to MUTV, Senne Lammens admitted the team had struggled early on but had done enough after the break to put themselves in a winning position.

“Football can be a bit cruel at times,” the Belgian goalkeeper said. “There are a lot of ups and downs, especially in a game like that.”

Senne Lammens felt United failed to take advantage of Tottenham’s red card, allowing the visitors too much space to find a late equaliser.

“We’ve won a lot of games against 10 men [in the past], but you also know there can be a tricky situation when you’re playing against 10 men, because they have nothing to lose and they know that.”

He added that United should have scored again to put the result beyond doubt or, at the very least, prevented Tottenham from creating further chances.

“I think that’s what we did wrong. We gave them a little bit too much breathing room to create those chances, and then one ball has to go right for them, one bounce has to go their way, and they can score like that.”

The goalkeeper also pointed to similarities with United’s earlier disappointment against Everton, where points slipped away late in the match.

“You feel like those games just slip away from you, and there are one or two situations where you don’t really have control,” he said.

“I think there’s a lot to learn from today. It wasn’t all negative, not at all, but especially the way it ended left a very bad feeling.”

“I think the easy answer is that we have to be able to kill the game faster and not put ourselves in that position to give them a chance.”

Despite the frustration, Lammens said there were positives to take from the performance. However, the late goal had left a bitter feeling, and United now need to turn those lessons into better results.

#2119. Michael Morrison reveals major Gianfranco Zola error at Birmingham City

Former Birmingham City captain Michael Morrison has revealed a major error which arose during Gianfranco Zola's ill-fated reign in charge at St. Andrew's @ Knighthead Park between December 2016 and April 2017.

Birmingham are currently a club on the up, with Chris Davies' side topping the Championship for the first time in 18 years over the course of the international break.

Even though Knighthead Capital Management have pumped millions of pounds into various aspects of the club, locals in this part of the Second City haven't lost sight of what was a previously torrid era.

Constant turnover of managers, players and ownership issues were major contributing factors to said demise, with Zola's short time at St. Andrew's epitomising such chaos, as Blues went from potential play-off contenders under to requiring a final-day relegation escape in the same season.

Zola was appointed as Gary Rowett's successor in December 2015 in rather controversial circumstances shortly after a takeover at St. Andrew's from Birmingham Sports Holdings Limited.

Birmingham were seventh in the Championship at the time when the former Chelsea icon and ex-West Ham United and Watford boss signed a two-and-a-half-year contract.

His first match in charge came two days later against high-flying Brighton and Hove Albion in a televised encounter, which Blues lost 2-1 despite taking the lead through Lukas Jutkiewicz.

Featuring on the 'Made in Brum' podcast, Morrison, who made 183 appearances for the club, has revealed that Zola made a glaring error in his first meeting with the players at Wast Hills.

"Sometimes you'd go 'Gianfranco Zola, this is going to be amazing', but in my experience, when you bring them people in, they need to have good people around them," Morrison explained.

"I didn't think he brought in very good staff around him, and that was part of the problem.

"In Gianfranco's first meeting, I remember meeting him and he said 'I'm not going to change too much in a short space of time, we'll see how it goes, we won't be out on the grass too long', and we were out on the grass for two hours, which is a long time to be out before a game, and then we conceded in the last minute.

"Straight away you're like 'you've flogged us there'. If you hadn't had done that, and that's when I talk about wins going by.

"I remember in the first meeting, he's talking about Brighton's team: 'they've got this player, that player. They've got Sam B*****s up front, and we're like 'don't you mean Sam Baldock', who was the Championship's top scorer at the time," the former Blues man added.

"Straight away you're kind of laughing, but if this guy is getting the top scorer wrong on his first day, you think it could be a disaster, and it turned out to be that."

Gary Rowett has revealed how he reacted to his shock sacking at Birmingham City in December 2016

As Morrison alluded to, Zola's reign was nothing short of disastrous, even though Birmingham had the crux of an experienced Championship side and attempted to add further quality in the January window with the additions of Emilio Nsue, Craig Gardner, Cheik Keita and Kerim Frei.

However, Zola won just two of his 24 matches in charge, with it taking 10 of those for the first victory to come against Fulham in February 2017.

Blues fans, where does Gianfranco Zola rank in the club's worst managerial appointments? Comment below!

He then resigned two months later after an Easter Monday defeat to Burton Albion, saying: "It is not that I like quitting, but Birmingham deserves better."

Since then, the Oliena native hasn't returned to management, whilst Harry Redknapp was appointed as his successor, although he, like Zola, would find his St. Andrew's tenure extremely short-lived.

Ultimately, Birmingham continued to go through several managers after Zola's exit, with multiple years of stagnation in the Championship resulting in a relegation to League One in May 2024, less than a year after Knighthead's takeover.

An even costlier decision was made during that particular season too, as John Eustace was sacked in October 2023 despite the fact Birmingham were sixth in the table, with high-profile replacement, Wayne Rooney, lasting less than three months in charge, winning just two of his 15 games.

However, the club's American investors have since learned from their own mistakes by keeping faith in Chris Davies, who has refined his tactical approach this season, and it has certainly got Birmingham fans dreaming of promotion after an extremely encouraging start.

#2118. Manchester United defence: Why Carrick must trust Yoro and Heaven

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United endured another embarrassing draw against 10-man Tottenham after failing to register their second win despite bringing in a plethora of players.

Manchester United invested heavily last season in their attacking options, bringing in Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha.

This season, they overhauled their midfield. United spent massively on Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos. Despite spending massively, they have failed to produce the control they would have expected in the midfield. The lack of control was evident in the recent Tottenham game, where Mainoo-Tielemans partnership failed to control the game collectively.

The midfield question was covered in our recent report as well, highlighting a lack of control and carried comments from Gary Neville and Jamie Redknapp.

The bigger question is when United will strengthen their defence. As per our previous report as well, Manchester United are planning to overhaul their defence in the upcoming transfer windows.

United were heavily linked with several left backs but eventually failed to bring any one. The situation left Luke Shaw as the only senior option in the position, while Patrick Dorgu is used upfront by Michael Carrick.

Harry Amass is another option for Michael Carrick, but he is only here because of a failed transfer move. He has been rarely used at left back as Dalot and Mazraoui get the nod in the position ahead of him.

The situation at right-back isn’t all good either. Diogo Dalot is the first option there, but he rarely provides the assurance that puts Michael Carrick at ease. Noussair Mazraoui is the second choice at right-back, but his attacking numbers aren’t great either.

Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez form up United’s centre-back pairing while Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven are used all over the defensive line in rotation when needed. Yoro was used at right-back against Tottenham while Heaven arrived as left-back towards the end of the game.

Manchester United’s season hasn’t been defensively strong or anywhere near being good. They have conceded goals in all Premier League games and only kept one clean sheet against Sabah in the Champions League.

Lisandro Martinez has come under scrutiny after errors on four occasions. Against Ipswich Town, Manchester United won 5-2, but his error resulted in Ipswich’s second goal.

His own goal against Fulham gave away two points at Craven Cottage in the 1-1 draw. Another error led to Solanke’s goal against Tottenham, when he took his eyes off the ball.

His injury concerns are another aspect, and maybe Michael Carrick needs to make a decision.

Manchester United’s success depended heavily on youth over the years. When pundits questioned them, Sir Alex Ferguson gave them the chance to prove them wrong. Alan Hansen made the famous quote “You can’t win anything with kids” on the BBC’s Match of the Day on August 19, 1995. United did exactly that, played youth and went on to win everything.

Michael Carrick needs to do exactly that. He needs to trust youth and allow them to make mistakes. Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven arrived as massive potentials, but they haven’t been given the license to express themselves, without fearing for their places. Both the youngsters have rarely started together or in a stretch of games. It is maybe time for them to take their chances.

Michael Carrick needs to keep Harry Maguire as a senior experienced figure around them. There is no doubt over Martinez’s ability, but he is not the answer to United’s long-term problem. United need to blend youth with experience as their identity moving forward. Lisandro Martinez perhaps isn’t the answer to United’s problem.

A defensive revival expected in the upcoming transfer windows needs to happen now. It must happen with chances to the Youth. Michael Carrick needs to be brave enough and throw the youngsters in the mix. What it will bring is a long-term solution. They need to experience the errors and pressures that will shape them in football.

#2116. Blackburn Rovers fans should be excited but worried at new Andri Gudjohnsen exploits

Blackburn have had a positive season under Tony Mowbray, with the side sitting in mid-table going into the international break.

Many had tipped Rovers to be fighting relegation before a ball was kicked this season, but they are just three points away from the play-off places, and they hold a healthy 11-point advantage above 22nd-placed Burnley.

So, all connected to Blackburn will be delighted at how the campaign has begun, and there will be a belief that they can maintain this form, especially due to the form of striker Andri Gudjohnsen.

Whilst it has been a team effort at Rovers, it’s hard not to single out Gudjohnsen, who is the son of former Chelsea man Eidur, for individual praise.

That’s because he has been superb in front of goal, scoring ten times in 14 games, with a shot conversion rate that is better than anyone in Europe, which includes the likes of Raphinha and Erling Haaland.

The 24-year-old is in the form of his career right now, and he continued that on international duty with Iceland on Friday night, as he scored a hat-trick in their 5-0 win at Bulgaria.

This was Gudjohnsen at his devastating best, as he was once again ruthless in front of goal, and it means he now has nine goals in his last six games in all competitions, which is a remarkable return.

Gudjohnsen will hope to extend his goalscoring run when Iceland host Luxembourg on Monday, but, for Blackburn fans, the focus will be on their big game against Burnley when club football returns.

Don Goodman's top three Championship strikers - has he missed anyone out?

This is the game that all Rovers fans would’ve looked for as soon as the fixtures were released, and Mowbray’s men will make the short trip to Turf Moor next weekend.

So, Blackburn will head to their bitter rivals with genuine confidence, and if they are to return home with all three points, you get the feeling that Gudjohnsen will have a significant role to play.

His form, combined with Burnley’s defensive woes, means the striker will fancy his chances of making a difference in the derby.

Of course, Gudjohnsen will be focused on Blackburn when he returns from international duty, and he will be determined to help the team close the gap on the top eight.

However, it’s unrealistic to think that his goalscoring exploits won’t have attracted attention, so the January window could be a challenge for Rovers.

Finding a number nine who can score goals is a major challenge for all clubs, but Gudjohnsen is proving himself to be someone who can do just that.

His ball-striking technique is superb, and Gudjohnsen is proving time and time again that his movement and anticipation is excellent, as he knows how to find space in and around the box.

Five players, five careers. Name them from the clubs they played for.

Each day there are five current or former EFL players to identify. For each one you’ll see their senior clubs in the order they played for them. Loan spells are left out.

Plus, he signed a new ‘long-term’ contract earlier this year, so Blackburn won’t be in a position where they have to cash in.
